reading.body:
Flexential Las Vegas - North publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 111,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 9 MW supports roughly 225 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, the same power supports roughly 900 racks. The operator has not published which density applies, so neither figure is a claim about actual rack count, only a boundary on what the power allows.

The certification stack qualifies this campus for specific regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 cover financial and operational controls audits. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for export-controlled defense technical data. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal security controls. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. SSAE 18 is the attestation standard underlying the SOC reports. Together these certifications open the facility to heavily regulated AI workloads in finance, defense, and healthcare, though which tenants occupy it is not published.

Within Nevada, this campus ranks first by published IT capacity, but that ranking reflects a data gap rather than dominance. This site has mapped 26 facilities in the state, and only one, this campus, has a published megawatt figure on its operator spec page. The remaining 25 mapped facilities publish no power figure, so the 9 MW total for Nevada reflects only what has been read here, not the true installed base in the state.
